$comment: capture-plan.json: which devices capture which screens in which locales, and how each screen is reached (CONTRACT.md 10.2). Paths are relative to the plan's own folder. Settings (locales, appearance, clock, statusBar, seed, flatten, posture) resolve plan, then the device, then the screen, then the screen's overrides for that device's platform, its layout, then its id (each later one wins). staging (agreed with the user first) and each screen's state and verify say how the app is set up and what each screen must show. Uses only the subset appstores_lib/schema.py validates.

out.$comment: The captures' folder: <out>/<locale>/<device id>/<screen id>.png and <out>/capture-report.json. Default 'captures'.

appSource.$comment: The app's source checkout, for what changed since the last capture (capture.py --changes) and the revision each shot was taken at (the report's app and appRevision): repo (its folder, relative to the plan; default the plan's own) and paths (the folders and files the staged screens are drawn by, relative to repo; with each screen's sources, what --changes looks at).

clock.$comment: The status bar's time: 'H:MM' or 'HH:MM' (24-hour), or an ISO date-time. Default '09:41'.

statusBar.$comment: clean: the plan's clock, full battery and signal, no notifications (simctl status_bar, Android's demo mode). as-is: left alone. Default clean.

seed.$comment: Passed to the app as ScreenshotSeed (a launch argument, an intent extra, a query parameter).

flatten.$comment: The colour a picture with an alpha channel is flattened onto (#RRGGBB). Default #000000, as a device's masked corners are.

posture.$comment: A foldable's posture before the steps: folded (the cover display), open (unfolded: the inner display), half-open (tabletop or book, target.hingeAngle, default 90). Android emulators through their console, real foldables through cmd device_state, the iPhone Duo simulator through DevFlow's fold control. Each posture captured is its own device in the plan (its own id and size).

stepName.$comment: A step's handle, for an override's stepsPatch to name it by.

stepRef.$comment: A step by its name, or by its 1-based position in the steps as they are when the patch entry runs (names survive edits; positions don't).

stepPatch.$comment: One change to the steps before it: prepend or append steps, remove a step, replace one with steps, insert steps before or after one.

app.$comment: The app on each platform. A device uses the entry for its platform, else its family's (ipados/tvos/watchos/visionos -> ios), merged with the device's own 'app'.
A built .app to install (simulators) or open (macOS).

processName.$comment: macOS: the process name System Events knows it by (default: the .app's name).

activity.$comment: The activity launch starts ('.MainActivity' or a full class name).

apk.$comment: An APK to install before the screens (adb install -r).

url.$comment: The app's address (on this machine: drivers reach nothing else). launch opens it; url steps resolve against it.

kind.$comment: phone, tablet, desktop, tv, watch or xr: which store slot its pictures are for (check_captures.py --rules).

layout.$comment: A name for how the app lays out on this device (wide, split, cover...): screens' overrides keyed by it apply to every device with it, after the platform's and before the device id's.

width.$comment: The exact pixel size this device promises (from the store's rules). Any other size is failed, never resized.

target.$comment: The driver's own settings (simctl: deviceType, runtime, udid, display (a screen id, or auto), localeScope, hingeAngle, foldCli, postureSettle; adb: systemImage, profile, avd, serial, wmSize, density, deviceLocale, display (a SurfaceFlinger display id, or auto), hingeAngle, navigation, statusBarMobile, statusBarCheck, adb, emulator, avdmanager; agents: agentPort, agentPlatform, appName, agentTimeout, host, screenshot; appium: server, capabilities (on a simulator the driver adds appium:isHeadless and the device's own appium:wdaLocalPort and appium:mjpegServerPort, from its id; a value set here is kept); chrome: scale, viewport, mobile; macos: scale). references/config.md lists them all.

app.$comment: Merged over the plan's app entry for this device's platform.

state.$comment: What the screen must show, in plain words (whose data, which state): agreed with the user; in staging.md and the report.

inUse.$comment: What this screen looks like in use, in plain words (the form part-filled: 12 servings, 45 minutes; the list with eight entries; or why it's empty on purpose): agreed with the user, in staging.md beside the values its fill and type steps enter.

sources.$comment: The app's files (or folders) that draw this screen, relative to appSource.repo: capture.py --changes names the screen when one changed since the last capture.

staging.$comment: false: this screen gets neither the staging's seed nor its launch values (an onboarding screen, say).

devices.$comment: Only these devices (ids). Default: every device.

locales.$comment: Only these of the device's locales.

overrides.$comment: Per device id, layout or platform: settings, steps or a patch to the steps that differ there ({"android": {"steps": [...]}}, {"wide": {"stepsPatch": [{"remove": "open-tab"}]}}). They apply platform, then layout, then device id.

steps.$comment: Replaces the steps before it (a whole copy: a later fix to the base steps doesn't reach it; prefer stepsPatch).

stepsPatch.$comment: Changes the steps before it, entry by entry, so the base steps' fixes still reach this device.

omit.$comment: Leave this screen out here (true, or why: 'the open Duo shows it beside the overview').

element.$comment: One of id (accessibility identifier / automation id / resource id / test id), text, label, xpath or css (web).

timeout.$comment: Seconds to wait for it. Default 10.

tapTarget.$comment: An element, or a point {x, y} in the picture's pixels.

keyboardTries.$comment: How to close the keyboard, tried in order until it's down: the driver's own (own: false leaves it out), done (the app's own Done or Close button: an element or {x, y}; Appium on iOS looks for one by name itself; a number pad has no key that closes it), scroll (true, a direction, or {direction, in}), then last tap (something neutral: a title or label, or {x, y}; many apps don't close the keyboard for it). Still up after all: the step fails, naming what was tried.

fillField.$comment: One field and what's typed into it: field is an element, or a string (its id).

scrollTo.$comment: An element, or an end: top or bottom.

elementCheck.$comment: An element to wait for or verify: one of id, text, label, xpath or css, and optionally contains (text the element shows, itself or anything under it: an iOS label, an Android child's text; ignoring case and runs of space).

timeout.$comment: Seconds to wait for it. Default 10 (a wait), 5 (verify).

appPath.$comment: A path inside the app's own data: iOS relative to its data container (Library/Caches/app.db), Android to /data/data/<package> (files/app.db, cache/app.db); one, or one per platform.

keyboardCheck.$comment: The on-screen keyboard: hidden (the default for a screen that types nothing, where the driver can tell), shown, or any (not checked).

verify.$comment: An element (or a list), and the keyboard's state, that must be so before the shot; otherwise the shot is missed, 'wrong state'. A driver that can't see elements reports it unchecked.

staging.$comment: How the app is staged for the captures, agreed with the user before the plan is run (references/staging.md). capture.py puts launch and seed into every screen, grants the permissions, checks the account's variables are set, and captures more than one screen only once confirmed is set; capture.py --write-staging writes it readable as staging.md.

doc.$comment: The readable copy beside the plan (default staging.md).

confirmed.$comment: Set when the user has seen one screen captured with this staging and agreed it. Until then a run captures one screen only.

account.$comment: How the app is signed in: none, guest (guest mode), bypass (a debug sign-in bypass) or demo (a demo account, its sign-in only by the names of environment variables; never a real person's account).

env.$comment: Variables holding the demo account's sign-in (DEMO_USER, DEMO_PASSWORD): checked before a run, usable in launch values as ${NAME}, masked in logs and reports.

seed.$comment: Where the demo data comes from: command (run before each screen, like a script step), file (copied into the app's own data before each screen, an appFile step), launch (the app seeds itself from a launch argument: put it in launch.args), backend (a staging server with invented data) or none.

when.$comment: each-screen (default) or once (before each device's first screen).

launch.$comment: Added to every launch step (a step's own args and env win): the screenshot mode's switch, a sign-in bypass, a fake server's address. ${NAME} takes one of account.env's variables.

skip.$comment: What's skipped and how: onboarding, paywalls, rating prompts, what's-new sheets, tooltips.

permissions.$comment: Granted before launch, revoked after, by platform: simctl privacy services on Apple (photos, location, contacts, ...), Android permission names (android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS).

flags.$comment: Feature flags the screens need, and how they're set (usually a launch arg).

clock.$comment: The app's own 'now' (the status bar's is the plan's clock) and how it's fixed. On-screen times usually need a screenshot mode; without one, pick screens that show none, or say so.

network.$comment: offline (fixtures), mock (a local fake server), staging (a staging server with invented data) or live (discouraged).

inUse.$comment: How the screens look in use, app-wide, as the user put it: forms partly filled with believable values, lists populated, no empty states or placeholder-only fields; nothing saved unless that's the point. Each screen's inUse says what it means there; rendered in staging.md and asked about for every new screen.

by.$comment: Who said it and when (the user, in chat, 2026-11-20).

values.$comment: What believable values are here (a mid-task user's: typical readings, invented names; never real people's).

save.$comment: false (the default): a filled form is captured before it's saved; true: saving is part of a screen's story.

notes.$comment: House rules for the captures that fit no other field, rendered in staging.md (a plan's $comment isn't).

args.$comment: Launch arguments (iOS -Key value), intent extras (Android), query parameters (web).

clean.$comment: Reinstall or clear the app's data first.

into.$comment: The field to type into, found by its text (placeholder).

to.$comment: An element (looked for in direction, default down, until it's in view or the content stops moving, then the other way), or top or bottom (until the content stops moving).

in.$comment: The element to scroll within (a pane of a two-pane layout, a list), else the screen's middle: the scroll view or anything inside it (its nearest scrolling ancestor is scrolled).

hold.$comment: With from and to: ms the finger stays down at from before it moves (a slider, a drag handle, a reorder, a custom pan gesture that reads a quick touch as a scroll). Default 0.

flow.$comment: A Maestro flow's path or a UI test's name (string), or the flow driver's own object.

appFile.$comment: Copy a file into the app's own data, the app stopped first (simctl's data container; Android's data folder through run-as, debug builds). Drivers with a host do it through the host.

posture.$comment: Fold, open or half-open the device in the middle of the steps (the device's or screen's posture does it before them).

hideKeyboard.$comment: Close the on-screen keyboard if it's up, trying the driver's own close (Android: back, only while it's up; Appium: mobile: hideKeyboard), the app's Done button, a scroll, then a tap on something neutral, in that order (keyboardTries).

unfocus.$comment: Clear the text field's focus so no caret blinks in the shot: true, or {tap: <element or {x, y}>} tapped first. Android: the keyboard closed, then Escape while a field has focus (checked); web: blur().

fill.$comment: Type into a form's fields in one step: each brought into view (both ways, within in), typed into, the keyboard closed before the next on Android; then the keyboard closed, the focus cleared and, with scrollTo, the form scrolled back. Nothing is submitted.

in.$comment: The pane the fields are in (scrolled within): the scroll view or anything inside it.

keyboard.$comment: true (default): closed after, as hideKeyboard; keep: left up (and the focus kept); or hideKeyboard's tries.

unfocus.$comment: Clear the focus after (default true, unless the keyboard's kept).

scrollTo.$comment: Then scroll back: top, bottom or an element (typing scrolls a long form).

ignore.$comment: Rectangles [x, y, width, height] in the picture's pixels left out of the comparison (an animation that never stops).
